title: Defining the Histopathological Extent of Resection of Brain Metastasis: HighResection Met (HiRes Met) – A Pilot Study
summary:
This study investigates whether, in brain metastases located in non-eloquent brain regions, it is possible to remove the tumor as completely as in other surgical fields, namely with a so-called safety margin (“R0 resection”). Until now, surgery has usually focused on removing only the tumor portion visible on MRI. However, it is known that tumor cells may also be present in the surrounding brain tissue.
To examine this, small tissue samples will be taken during surgery from the tumor margins and adjacent brain tissue and immediately analyzed by an experienced neuropathologist. The surgeon will then receive direct feedback on whether tumor cells are still present or whether healthy tissue has already been reached. This information helps the surgeon decide whether to terminate or continue the resection.
The aim of this pilot study is to determine whether this approach is feasible and meaningful, and whether it may serve as the basis for a larger study investigating the potential impact of such an R0 resection on patient survival and quality of life.
conditions: Secondary malignant neoplasm of brain and cerebral meninges

interventions.name: Non-eloquent metastases (supramaximal resection + intraoperative histopathological assessment of resection margins)
